Create a lazy whole-sample NIS survey design

Source: R/lazy-survey.R
nis_survey.Rd

The nested, one-stage Taylor design uses hospital-year PSUs (YEAR × HOSP_NIS) and year-specific strata (YEAR × NIS_STRATUM), without a finite population correction. It uses the valid-design discharges in the input query. Apply eligibility restrictions with dplyr::filter() on the design so hospitals outside the domain still contribute to variance. Use subset() as the survey-style alternative. A query filtered before construction defines a different sample.

Usage

nis_survey(.data, weights = DISCWT)

Arguments

.data

A lazy DuckDB query from nis_open().

weights

A data-masked SQL-translatable expression for the analysis weights. The default uses discharge weights without annualization.

Value

A lazy nis_survey design.

Details

Use survey::svymean(), survey::svytotal(), or survey::svyby() with one-sided formulas. Grouped estimates support means and totals. Use survey::svyglm() for additive models with Gaussian identity, binomial or quasibinomial logit, and Poisson or quasipoisson log families. Wald inference uses the sample design degrees of freedom minus the fitted model rank plus one. DuckDB computes weighted sums by PSU without collecting discharge records. The analysis supports the "fail" and "adjust" values of survey.lonely.psu and honors survey.adjust.domain.lonely. Use nis_design() for row-level operations such as quantiles, chi-square tests, model diagnostics, and gtsummary::tbl_svysummary().

Discharges with missing, non-finite, or nonpositive design fields (YEAR, HOSP_NIS, NIS_STRATUM, or DISCWT) are excluded. Custom analysis weights must be positive and finite within the domain.

See also

Other survey-design: nis_design(), nis_reweight()

Examples

nis <- nis_open(nis_example(2019:2020))
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpfXkzhU/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpfXkzhU/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
design <- nis_survey(nis)
older <- dplyr::filter(design, AGE >= 65)
survey::svymean(~LOS, older)
#>       mean     SE
#> LOS 4.5771 0.2929
survey::svyby(~LOS, ~YEAR, older, survey::svymean)
#>      YEAR      LOS        se
#> 2019 2019 4.577143 0.4142243
#> 2020 2020 4.577143 0.4142243
